thread:
ana: Hey team, planning a move to Valencia (Spain) for a 10-week family sabbatical starting late August. Do we need to change homebase or can I stay on US payroll? Curious about WFH stipend, social security/health impacts, and whether I should expect any tax withholding changes.

diego: Love Valencia! :sun_with_face: Short version: depends on number of days and tax residency rules. If <183 days and no local employment, sometimes employees remain on US payroll, but need to confirm with payroll/legal.

nora (People Ops): Please submit the short-term remote form (link in automated message). We treat sabbaticals differently than full relocations. Will check benefits portability.

sam (Benefits): If your US medical plan has international coverage, claims may be possible but higher out-of-network costs. For Spain, EU rules might require local public health registration if you become tax resident. Send your expected dates and address.

ben (Payroll): Quick ask: will you be doing any contracting/paid work for a Spanish entity or clients while there? Also need to know if family members will be working locally.

ana: No contracting. spouse is remote and still on US payroll as well. We're both staying with family in Valencia.

ben (Payroll): OK. We'll run a 2-scenario simulation: (A) remain on US payroll (with potential local reporting) (B) cutover to Spain payroll. Likely outcome: remain on US payroll if under 183 days, but we still need to check municipal/local regulations and social security.

nora (People Ops): WFH stipend: policy allows monthly stipend while working remotely. For short-term international stays we apply a cap of 3 months at full stipend; after that we review. Since you're 10 weeks, you should be fine for full stipend prorated by days. Keep receipts for coworking if you want reimbursement for membership.

legal-bot: Note: any stay >90 days can trigger local registration requirements in some EU jurisdictions. Please confirm exact dates.

ana: Dates: depart US 2024-08-24, arrive 2024-08-25, return 2024-10-31.

diego: Since return is Oct 31 you cross 90-day threshold for Schengen stays in a calendar period? Check visa rules. Not a tax expert though.

sam (Benefits): Also verify evacuation/repatriation coverage if included in policy; travel medical is different.

ben (Payroll): We'll need: passport copy, address in Spain, last US paystub, estimated days in-country. Expect a decision in ~5 business days after intake.

nora (People Ops): Sending short-term remote form link now. Please mark "sabbatical" and attach travel itinerary.

ana: Form submitted (ID 1720056789). Attachments uploaded. Thanks!

people-ops-bot: Short-term-remote-guidelines.pdf uploaded: https://rwd.internal/people-ops/short-term-remote (automated)

ben (Payroll): After simulation: if you stay on US payroll and need to file local taxes, Redwood will provide a tax advisory partner contact but any local filings remain employee responsibility unless we cut over payroll. If cutover, we'll handle withholding and statutory benefits.

ana: Any change to 401(k) or stock vesting?

sam (Benefits): 401(k) contributions typically stop if you switch to a local payroll. If you remain on US payroll contributions continue. Equity vesting unaffected by location but check with comp ops for tax implications on local withholding for exercises/awards.

nora (People Ops): If you'd like us to request temporary coworking budget beyond stipend (e.g., dedicated desk for 10 weeks), tag me and provide cost estimate. We'll review.

ana: Tagging nora for coworking request: coworking estimate €120/month, total €300 for 10 weeks? (approx).

nora (People Ops): Thanks — attach invoice and we'll consider.

legal-bot: Reminder: Do not accept local employment or invoice clients. That creates employer nexus.

ben (Payroll): Intake call scheduled Wed 9am PT. Invite sent.

ana: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
